content.text: The garden that wakes after dark
Paths glow softly under indigo sky. Fragrant night-blooming flowers open, moths drift between lanterns, and the air cools into something quieter and more intimate than day.

content.text: Four quiet zones
Each area of the Night Garden has its own light, scent and pace. Move slowly between them.

content.text: Moonlit Path
A long gravel walk lined with white evening primrose and silver foliage. Soft ground lights mark the edges without spoiling the dark.

content.text: Fragrance Court
Night-scented stock, jasmine and tuberose release their strongest perfume after dusk. Benches face inward so conversation stays soft.

content.text: Shadow Grove
Mature trees and understory ferns create deep shade even at night. Ideal for those who prefer cooler air and fewer lanterns.

content.text: Reflecting Pool
Still water mirrors the sky and a few carefully placed water lilies. Visitors are asked to keep silence here after 21:00.

content.text: Night-blooming collections
Explore by scent, form or season. Each tab gathers plants that share a character after sunset.
Fragrance first

Evening primrose, night-scented stock and jasmine open their strongest perfume once the air cools. We keep these beds away from the main paths so the scent can pool rather than disperse. Guests often pause here longer than they expect.
Best experienced between 20:30 and 22:00 on still evenings.
Shape and silhouette

Tall spires of Verbascum, the architectural leaves of cardoon, and the soft mounds of lamb’s ear catch the low lantern light. These plants are chosen as much for how they read in near-darkness as for daytime interest.
Look for the silver and white foliage near the Moonlit Path.
What is open now

Late summer brings the heaviest scent load; early autumn shifts toward seed heads and structural grasses. Winter openings feature evergreens, frost on the pool, and a smaller set of heated glasshouses for tender night bloomers.
Check the evening programme for current flowering highlights.

content.text: Before you arrive
A few simple guidelines keep the Night Garden calm for everyone and for the plants.
Gates open one hour after sunset and close at midnight. Last entry is 22:30. On clear nights we sometimes extend the final half-hour for those already inside.
Entry is by timed ticket only. We limit numbers so paths never feel crowded. Children under 12 enter free with an adult; groups larger than six should contact us in advance.
Comfortable shoes for gravel and soft ground, a light layer for cooler air, and a small torch if you prefer. Flash photography is not allowed near the Reflecting Pool or in the Fragrance Court.

The main Moonlit Path and Fragrance Court are step-free with firm surfaces. The Shadow Grove has uneven ground and is best avoided with mobility aids. A quiet rest space with seating is available near the entrance.

Stay on marked paths, do not pick flowers or leaves, and keep voices low after 21:00. Dogs are welcome on short leads on the outer circuit only; they are not allowed near the pool or in the Fragrance Court.

content.text: Evenings this season
Small gatherings that match the pace of the garden — never loud, never crowded.
Every Thursday
Silent Walk
A guided hour without speaking. Lanterns are minimal; the focus is on sound, scent and the feel of the path underfoot.
First Saturday
Night Botany
A short talk on how certain plants time their opening to moths and cooler temperatures, followed by time to observe the current blooms.
Clear nights only
Pool Reflections
Sit by the Reflecting Pool with a single cup of tea. No programme — only the sky, the water and the quiet.
Late October
Season Close
One final evening before winter hours begin. Longer access, a small outdoor reading of seasonal notes, and the last heavy scent of the year.

content.text: Come after dark
Timed tickets open three weeks ahead. Choose a clear evening if you can — the garden rewards patience and soft footsteps.
